rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 1 line 6: 'This is a 1983 argument, not an AI take.' — the demonstrative is cataphoric framing resolved by the rest of the same bullet and chunk (Bainbridge's finding, named one clause later in the same sentence). Line 7 'Both jobs' <- 'the human keeps two jobs' named line 6, same chunk. Line 8 'those reps' <- 'the reps of doing the task yourself' named line 7, same chunk. Chunk 2 line 13 'named this **overreliance**' <- resolved by the immediately preceding clause in the same sentence ('your own detection performance degrades'). Line 14 'the agent' is the first literal appearance of that noun IN THIS FILE, but it is arc-earned spine vocabulary: `grep -rn "\bthe agent\b" curriculum/exercises/*.md curriculum/lectures/*.md | grep -v ironies-of-automation` returns hits from `audit-your-agent.md`, `author-security-skill.md` and dozens more, and `getting-going.md` (the training's M1 file) exists and uses the term from the opening module — this M4-closing lecture sits many modules downstream of where 'the agent' became baseline vocabulary, so the carve-out for the training's own named terms once earned in a prior module applies; it does not need re-introduction on this slide. Closest-to-violating candidate: line 15 'The same observed competence' — resolves cleanly to 'trust'/'competence' named in the header (line 10) and prior bullets of the same chunk, no gap.

Read every sentence in lines 1-16: no phrase points at another file, module, or prior slide by position (no 'the opening lecture said', 'that story', 'earlier we saw'). Attributions are all by name ('Lisanne Bainbridge', 'the automation-studies literature ... Parasuraman and Riley') — citation of a named source, not a positional callback to another curriculum file. No candidate approaches this rule.

Chunk 1 (lines 3-9) carries 3 substantive bullets on the two-jobs/atrophy mechanism; chunk 2 (lines 10-16) carries 3 substantive bullets on the trust/vigilance mechanism and closes with a standalone question. Neither is a bare wait-state or a single context-dependent bullet. Chunk 0 (line 1, the H1) is the title slide with no `##` content of its own and is not scored as a content chunk under this rule.

Chunk 1 header 'Monitoring and takeover run on the same reps' (line 3) is proven by lines 6-8: two jobs (monitor, take over), both riding on 'the reps of doing the task yourself' (line 7) — a literal match. Chunk 2 header 'Trust and vigilance move in opposite directions' (line 10) is restated near-verbatim as the chunk's own line 15 opener — the strongest possible self-carry. Neither chunk's content contradicts its header.

`awk 'NR>=1 && NR<=16' curriculum/lectures/ironies-of-automation.md | grep -inE 'Not [A-Z][a-z]+\. Not '` -> exit 1, zero hits: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction. Anaphora check: line 14 has two 'The more X, the worse Y' clauses ('The more tasks the agent lands cleanly...' / 'The more autonomy the agent earns...') but they are separated by a differently-shaped middle sentence, not three consecutive identical-stem clauses, and each carries distinct concrete content (tasks landing vs. autonomy earned) — not the banned triple shape. No self-grading superlative anywhere (the file never grades its own usefulness). Only number present is the plain citation date '1983' (line 6), never hedged or retracted. 'hands-on fluency' (line 7) and 'detection performance' (line 13) are ordinary terms carried from the cited literature, not invented abstraction-stacking. Longest verb chain is the two-verb pair 'Monitor... Take over' (line 6) — no empty-leg triplet anywhere.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a lecture file, so both `##` headings must be claims, not imperatives/labels. Line 3 'Monitoring and takeover run on the same reps' and line 10 'Trust and vigilance move in opposite directions' are both full declarative sentences stating the slide's law, not orientation headers or catalogue-entry labels. Both are content the chunk itself proves out (cross-checked under rule 6).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked all 6 body bullets (lines 6-8, 13-15) against the three low-value classes. None is doctrine restatement of a repo-vocabulary split/lens/law re-announced with nothing added — every bullet advances the mechanism. None is self-referential design commentary about the curriculum being a pedagogy. Closest candidate for the aphorism-kicker class: line 15 opens 'Trust and vigilance move in opposite directions' — a near-verbatim echo of the chunk-2 header (line 10) — but rather than closing on that echo, the bullet continues into new load-bearing content (the mechanism sentence, 'The trust is deserved. The watching still has to be engineered.', and the lecture's one closing question) which the backing block names as 'the lecture's own synthesis, and the sentence the title is built on' (backing claim `trust-vigilance-opposite`) and 'the design's own move, and deliberately the only thing the lecture asks the student to do' (backing claim `ask-when-by-hand`). The bullet earns its slot; it is not a kicker restating the header with nothing else attached.
